setup: Lie on your back, arms by your sides
Lift your knees over your hips, bent to 90°
Palms resting lightly on the floor
execution: Curl your hips up off the floor toward your ribs
Roll your lower back up; knees stay bent
Pause, then lower your hips slowly
Stop when your knees are back over your hips
faults: Don't swing your legs for momentum
Don't let your knees drop past your hips
Don't shove the floor hard with your hands

notes: This is a small movement: the pelvis curls toward the ribs. Swinging the legs turns it into a hip exercise.
Lower under control so your lower back doesn't drop onto the floor.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Dead bug
regressions.reason: Builds control of the lower back and pelvis without curling.

progressions.name: Decline reverse crunch
progressions.reason: Head-up on a decline bench adds range and difficulty.

progressions.name: Captain's chair knee raise
progressions.reason: Same pelvic curl with the legs hanging; harder.

progressions.name: Hanging knee raise
progressions.reason: Same pelvic curl while hanging; harder and adds grip.

substitutions.name: Lying leg raise
substitutions.reason: Straight-leg hip lift on the floor; more hip work, less curl.

substitutions.name: Crunch
substitutions.reason: Curls from the ribs down instead.

substitutions.name: Cable crunch
substitutions.reason: Loaded ab curl with stack steps.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at floor level, figure lying along the frame with the head on the left. A thin mat line under the body.

keyPositions.label: Start
keyPositions.describe: Lying on the back, arms by the sides with palms down. Hips bent about 90° so the knees sit over the hips, knees bent about 90°. Lower back on the mat.

keyPositions.label: Curled
keyPositions.describe: Hips and lower back rolled up off the mat, knees drawn toward the chest, knee bend unchanged. Upper back, head and arms stay on the mat.

ikHints: Shoulders, head and hands stay on the mat in every frame
Knee angle stays about the same
emphasise: The pelvis curls up toward the ribs
Knees stay bent; legs don't swing

sources.title: ACE press release (2001): ACE-sponsored study reveals best and worst abdominal exercises
sources.supports: secondaryMuscles (reverse crunch ranked among the top three for oblique EMG in a 30-person study)
sources.note: Press release, not a peer-reviewed paper. Muscle activity is not the same as growth.

uncertain.note: The catalogue has no hip_flexors muscle word (expansion research Q1); ACE lists the hip flexors as assisting. They are left out rather than mapped to another muscle.
Approximate drawing targets, not measured data. pelvisLift is the tilt of the pelvis off the floor.
